content.text: {"answers": [{"question_id": "Q1", "question": "What event or condition triggers the scheduling of a vendor meeting — is it recurring on a fixed schedule, initiated by an internal request, or prompted by a specific operational event such as equipment underperformance?", "answer": "Triggered by an improvement request or equipment issue summary."}, {"question_id": "Q2", "question": "Which specific roles or job functions are expected to attend the vendor meeting, and which role is responsible for producing the post-meeting summary?", "answer": "Equipment engineer and vendor representative attend. Meeting organizer produces the summary."}, {"question_id": "Q3", "question": "Is there a defined template or structured format that must be followed when writing the meeting summary, or is it created in free-form using whatever tool the author prefers?", "answer": "Not specified."}, {"question_id": "Q4", "question": "How are action items captured and assigned during or after the meeting — for example, are they recorded in a spreadsheet, a project management tool, or an email thread, and who is responsible for assigning ownership and due dates?", "answer": "Recorded in an action-item tracker. Manager assigns owners and due dates."}, {"question_id": "Q5", "question": "What method is used to follow up on open action items — are reminders sent manually, through an automated system, or via scheduled review meetings, and is there an escalation path if an item is overdue?", "answer": "Action-item owner tracks progress. Automated reminders are an identified opportunity. Escalation not specified."}, {"question_id": "Q6", "question": "What criteria must be met for the entire follow-up process to be considered complete — does every action item need to be individually closed and confirmed, or is there a sign-off step by a specific role?", "answer": "Not specified."}]}
